questions.question: 6. Selection of circuit breaker depends upon:

answers.b: (Current under normal condition) + (maximum current which flows momentarily)
answers.c: (Current under normal condition) + (maximum current which flows momentarily) + (interrupting current at given kV)

explanations.a: Incomplete. Normal current alone is insufficient.
explanations.c: Correct. Circuit breaker selection considers normal current, momentary (making) current, and interrupting (breaking) capacity at rated voltage.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Short circuit current has both AC and DC components.
explanations.c: Correct. Short circuit current consists of symmetrical AC component and a DC offset (transient) component.

questions.question: 8. If θ ≅ 90 degree and α = 0, then maximum momentary current (i<sub>mm</sub>) will be:

answers.a: Half the maximum of symmetrical short circuit current
answers.b: Equal to the maximum of symmetrical short circuit current
answers.c: Four times to the maximum of symmetrical short circuit current
answers.d: Twice the maximum of symmetrical short circuit current

explanations.d: Correct. When θ ≈ 90° (purely inductive circuit) and α = 0 (fault at voltage zero crossing), the DC offset is maximum and peak momentary current is approximately 2 × √2 × I symmetrical peak = 2 × maximum symmetrical current.

questions.question: 9. The value of symmetrical short circuit current:

explanations.a: Correct. Symmetrical short circuit current (rms) = V / |Z|, and √2 V/|Z| is the peak value.

questions.question: 10. The effective value of transient reactance when there is no damping current:

explanations.d: Correct. Transient reactance Xd' = XL (armature leakage) + (Xa || Xf) where Xa is armature reaction reactance and Xf is field winding reactance.
